rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING ALL CORRECTIONAL, CUSTODIAL, AND DETENTION FACILITIES TO IMPLEMENT A CONTRABAND DETECTION AND CONTROL SYSTEM, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR POSSESSING, INTRODUCING, OR AIDING AND ABETTING THE ENTRY OF CONTRABAND INSIDE SUCH FACILITIES
rows.abstract:
Aims to implement stringent measures to regulate the entry of persons and things in correctional, custodial, and detention facilities, to prevent the entry of contraband inside such facilities, and to provide sanctions for violations of rules and regulations regarding the entry of contraband in these facilities.
Establishes the Contraband Detection and Control System (CDCS) that shall include the use of modern technology, devices, or units such as handheld and walk-through metal detectors, X-ray scanners, and K9 units to assist in the implementation of this Act.
Requires visitors and other persons entering the facilities to accomplish a registration form and present valid identification cards (ID) before or during the actual visit.
Enumerates the prohibited acts and the appropriate penalties for violation in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
Proposes to prohibit several items inside correctional, custodial, and detention facilities, among others:  
Any ammunition, firearm, weapons (R.A.10591); Explosives or incendiary devices (P.D. 1866, as amended by R.A. 09516); Dangerous drugs, illegal substances. . . & other paraphernalia (R.A.9165); Dangerous or deadly weapons; Alcoholic or intoxicating beverages; Cigarettes and other tobacco products (heated tobacco products (HTP), nicotine/non-nicotine, vapor/vaporized products (R.A. 11900), all forms of currency and monetary instruments; Electronic communication devices (cellphones, laptops, personal computers, digital devices); Signal jammers/devices (radio signals and transmissions); Luxury items (appliances, gambling/gaming equipment, jewelry); Object that is capable of threatening the safety, security, or health of persons . . . capable of aiding/executing the escape from such facilities.

rows.author: G078;K110;K070;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ENHANCE CITIZENS' ACCESS TO GOVERNMENT INFORMATION AND SERVICES BY REQUIRING ALL GOVERNMENT OFFICES TO ADOPT PLAIN LANGUAGE IN ALL ITS WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS TO THE PUBLIC, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims for a more responsive, accessible, and understandable government communication with the public founded on principles of transparency, public participation, and collaboration; Intends to provide an effective engagement and understanding in all government offices to adopt the use of plain language in English, Filipino and or other regional languages
Proposes that documents written in plain language that are inherently complex and, therefore, more accessible to all, including those with limited literacy skills; Seeks to include the Anti-Red Tape Authority, Governance Commission for GOCCs (GCG), DILG, AND PIA among the agencies that the CSC is mandated to collaborate with in implementing this Act.
rows.alias_name: Communication and Language Effectiveness for Accessible and Responsive (CLEAR) Government Act”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2023-09-20
